free_tier.stated: Volumes: 'Volumes include up to 1 TiB free' on the Starter plan, then $0.09/GiB/mo (per PricingSaaS capture of the Jun 2026 pricing change). Starter also includes $30/mo of compute.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: 500,000 inodes per Volume; 1 TiB free per workspace; volumes snapshot once/day for billing (deleted data can bill up to 4 days); $30/mo compute is the real ceiling — serving costs CPU-seconds, so throughput is bounded by the credit, not the disk.

egress.terms: 1 TiB/billing cycle included on Starter, then $0.04/GiB — metered but with a 1 TiB monthly floor. Explicitly: 'Reads from and writes to Modal Volumes do not count as network egress.'

tooling: `modal` Python SDK + `modal volume put/get/ls` CLI; volumes mount as a POSIX filesystem inside containers. Anyone who needs S3 semantics writes a tiny FastAPI shim on a web endpoint.
chaining: 1 TiB free volume per workspace x N free workspaces (Starter allows 3 users/workspace, workspaces themselves are free) => multi-TiB at zero cost. Each TiB is fully read-write and persists with no session attached.
